title: Is that Airbnb
worth buying?
lines: s1
Is that Airbnb actually worth buying? Let's run the numbers in EquityFoundry, in under a minute.
s2
Pick short-term rental. Enter the price and your closing costs. Furnishing counts too, so it's in the numbers.
s3
Now the nights. Nightly rate, occupancy, and average stay. Add the cleaning fee you charge, what cleaning costs you, and the platform's cut.
s4
Add your loan, then taxes, insurance, utilities and supplies. Vacancy and repairs are already built in.
s5
Here's your answer. Monthly cash flow. Cash-on-cash return. And revenue per night booked, after every single cost.
s6
Now test a slow season. Drop occupancy to fifty two percent and watch the cash flow update.
s7
Save it, compare it with your other deals, and know before you buy. EquityFoundry. Link in bio.

title: Pull your cash
back out?
lines: s1
Can you pull your cash back out of a rental? That's the BRRRR method. Here's how to check one in under a minute.
s2
Pick BRRRR. Enter the purchase price, the rehab budget, and your closing costs.
s3
Now the key number. The after-repair value, what the home is worth once it's fixed. Add how many months the rehab takes.
s4
Then the refinance. The loan-to-value your lender allows, the new rate, and the closing costs on the new loan.
s5
Add the rent you expect once the work is done, then your purchase loan. Taxes and insurance go in last.
s6
Here's your answer. Cash flow after the refinance. Cash left in the deal. And the equity you created. The less cash left in, the stronger the BRRRR.
s7
Save it, compare it with your other deals, and forge better deals. EquityFoundry. Link in bio.

title: Will this flip
make money?
lines: s1
Will this flip actually make money? Check it in under a minute with EquityFoundry.
s2
Pick fix and flip. Enter the purchase price, your repair budget, and your closing costs.
s3
Now the after-repair value, what it sells for once it's finished. Add how many months you'll hold it, and your selling costs.
s4
Add the loan carrying it. Then taxes, insurance and utilities, because you pay them while you hold.
s5
Here's your answer. Projected profit. Return on investment. And annualized return, so you can compare a flip to a rental.
s6
Check the seventy percent rule. It shows the most you should offer. Offer too high? Lower the price and watch the profit climb.
s7
Save it, compare it with your other deals, and know before you buy. EquityFoundry. Link in bio.

title: The 1% rule says yes.
